identity.symptom: sighup terminates prepared cli without shutdown diagnostics and leaves owned descendants

what: Prepared dev exits abruptly on terminal hangup and leaves its owned backend, inspector, and storage worker running.
expected: Native SIGHUP enters invocation cancellation, records shutdown diagnostics, joins all owned resources, and returns signal exit status 129.
observed: Actual prepared HTTP and inspector readiness passed; SIGHUP then returned native signal exit -1 without shutdown diagnostics, leaving three owned descendants. The unit test found no invocation SIGHUP listener.
root_cause: invocation-signals.ts:13 installed INT/TERM but no HUP owner; snapshot-session-options.ts:42 disables manual-session handlers in favor of that invocation owner. A prepared SIGHUP therefore bypassed Scope release, killed the proxy CLI, and orphaned its backend, inspector and storage worker. During initial/ordinary startup, main-support.ts:isFailure and the CliFailure/CliFailureError contracts also rejected HUP metadata, replacing the original reason/status129 with generic status130.
fixed_by: Verified native HUP invocation cancellation and its typed public failure contract. Both owners now preserve SIGHUP/status129, join resource cleanup and remove their own listeners. The prepared native replay and actual e-commerce HUP test close all owned processes/listeners; the final detached preview retains its eventual native exit code via a lightweight owner receipt.

invariants: Catchable native shutdown signals join owned children

environment.monitoring: Existing native CLI lifecycle, candidate, cleanup and HTTP logs plus owned process-table snapshots. No external crash-tracker evidence establishes the original stop signal. Bun1.3.10 and Effect4.0.1; all workload serialized, worker1 and nice15.
